meta.description: A self-hosting handbook: the fundamentals, a setup path in seven stages and Compose templates tailored to your domain, paths and reverse proxy.
lang.name: English
banner.label: Work in progress
banner.text: yourhomelab isn't finished yet. Many guides are still missing, and templates may change.
home.title: Your own server. Step by step.
home.lead: yourhomelab explains the fundamentals, walks you through the setup in seven stages and provides Compose files for the services you want to run. Tailored to your domain, your paths and your reverse proxy.
home.door1.title: Understand
home.door1.text: Concepts and background, organized like a wiki. For when you want to know why something works the way it does.
home.door2.title: Build
home.door2.text: Seven stages from an empty machine to a running homelab. You can tick off every step.
home.door3.title: Run
home.door3.text: Compose files for {n} services that adapt to your domain, paths and reverse proxy.
home.homelabsLead: How do others run theirs? From a single mini PC to a cluster: browse real setups and show your own.
home.faqLead: What yourhomelab is, what it isn't, and where else to find help.
home.decideText: Three questions about your internet connection, your data and your hardware. Afterwards you'll know where your server should live.
home.contributeText: All guides and Compose templates are openly available in the repository. Found a mistake or missing a service? Send a pull request or open an issue.
home.supportText: yourhomelab is free and ad-free. If a guide saved you time, the project appreciates a small donation.
oneway.title: One way among many
oneway.text: yourhomelab describes one possible setup: specific tools, conventions and directory structures. There are many other good ways, and you can shape your setup differently at any time. Guides and templates do build on each other, though, and work best if you stick to the conventions described here.
wiki.title: Learn
wiki.lead: Concepts and background on self-hosting. Pick a topic from the list or start with the fundamentals.
wiki.notYetText: We don't cover Kubernetes, k3s, Docker Swarm, Ansible and Terraform yet. Everything here builds on one server running Docker Compose.
page.stubText: The page exists, the content doesn't yet. Know your way around this topic? Write it directly on GitHub, the file is already there.
page.untranslated: This page hasn't been translated yet. You're seeing the original German version.
setup.title: Set up
setup.lead: Seven stages from an empty machine to a running homelab. The stages build on each other, and you can tick off every guide.
services.title: Services
services.lead: Every service comes with a tested compose.yaml and .env. The files adapt to your setup before you copy them.
services.missingText: Suggest it on GitHub or submit a template directly as a pull request.
homelabs.title: Homelabs
homelabs.lead: How other people run their homelab, from a single mini PC to a Kubernetes cluster. Every setup is one way among many, and none of them is the one right way.
homelabs.exampleNote: This entry is an example by yourhomelab, not a real person's homelab.
homelabs.submitText: Fill in the form on GitHub and we'll turn it into an entry. It doesn't matter how big or small your setup is.
service.forcedSub: {name} only works on its own subdomain, so the template uses a subdomain instead of a path URL.
service.networkText: Only for your first service: create the shared proxy network. If it already exists, skip this command.
service.step2Text: Copy the files into the folder. Random values for passwords and keys are already filled into the .env, generated only in your browser.
service.step3Text: Docker pulls the images and starts all containers of the stack.
service.upstreamText: The project's official Compose file. It is not tailored to your setup.
service.contributeText: Mistake in the template or a new version? Improve it directly on GitHub.
proxy.caddy.desc: One entry per service in the Caddyfile
proxy.npm.desc: Proxy host in the web interface
proxy.none.desc: Publish ports directly on the server
setupDialog.title: My setup
setupDialog.lead: These values flow into every command, compose.yaml and .env file. They stay in your browser only.
quiz.hint: Answer all questions to see the recommendation.
